ICON-2I Weather Forecast¶

⚠️ Deprecated: icon-2i.zarr will be retired on 21 October 2026. From that day it is no longer updated or available.

Use icon-2i-forecast-3-day.zarr instead: the same ICON-2I runs by ItaliaMeteo-ARPAE, with every variable of the run, on the surface and on pressure levels. Variable names and some units differ; its notebook shows how to read them.

Zarrified ICON-2I surface fields forecast, run by ItaliaMeteo-ARPAE at ~2.2 km resolution over Italy.

The store keeps a rolling window of the most recent forecast runs (dimension init_time), each extending 72 hours ahead in hourly steps (dimension lead_time), with valid_time = init_time + lead_time. Available variables: t2m (2 m temperature, K) and tp (total precipitation accumulated since the forecast start, mm).

Unlike the radar archives, old forecast runs are rotated out of this store, so always select runs relative to the end of the init_time axis (as done below) rather than by a fixed date.

In [1]:
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

ds = xr.open_dataset(dataset_url, engine="zarr")

Latest forecast run¶

In [4]:
run = ds.isel(init_time=-1)
str(run.init_time.values)
Out[4]:
'2026-09-23T12:00:00.000000000'

2 m temperature at +24 h¶

In [5]:
t2m_c = run["t2m"].sel(lead_time=np.timedelta64(24, "h")) - 273.15
t2m_c.plot(robust=True, cmap="RdYlBu_r", figsize=(8, 7))
Out[5]:
<matplotlib.collections.QuadMesh at 0x772a86c0bce0>

Forecast evolution¶

In [6]:
leads = [np.timedelta64(h, "h") for h in (0, 24, 48, 72)]
(run["t2m"].sel(lead_time=leads) - 273.15).plot(
    col="lead_time", robust=True, cmap="RdYlBu_r"
)
Out[6]:
<xarray.plot.facetgrid.FacetGrid at 0x772a869c25a0>

Point meteogram — Rome¶

In [8]:
every3h = slice(None, None, 3)
t2m_pt = (
    run["t2m"]
    .sel(latitude=41.9, longitude=12.5, method="nearest")
    .isel(lead_time=every3h)
    - 273.15
)
valid = run["valid_time"].isel(lead_time=every3h).values

plt.figure(figsize=(9, 4))
plt.plot(valid, t2m_pt, marker="o")
plt.title("2 m temperature forecast — Rome")
plt.ylabel("°C")
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
